abstract: | 
 Schools are key spaces of meritocratic socialization, yet little is known about how students conceive meritocracy and how these conceptions relate to the acceptance of privilege. Using an instrument previously applied to adults, we surveyed Chilean students in 6th and 9th grade (Wave 1: N = 846) and again in 7th and 10th grade (Wave 2: N = 662). Results support four distinct dimensions of beliefs, equivalent across waves but only partially across school stages. Endorsing meritocracy did not imply rejecting privilege: about one third of students held both positions, although their latent association was weak and inconsistent across groups. Latent means did not change significantly over one year. Secondary students were more skeptical than primary students about whether effort is rewarded, a cross-sectional contrast limited by item non-equivalence. The study offers a conceptual and measurement foundation for research on the development of these beliefs and their educational implications.
  
 \medskip
 
 **Keywords**: Meritocracy · Privilege · Schools · Measurement invariance · Socialization · Chile
